title: Dumbara mat
summary: Weave a geometric mat on a frame loom, packing each weft row with the comb.
howToPlay: Look at the lit mat in its frame: it shows the pattern the finished mat must have.
Tap a colour to lay the next crossing along the row; the gold square marks the place, and the reed comb rides against the last woven row.
The cotton threads not yet woven hang bare below the comb. Undo takes back the last crossing.
Press Check to see your stars, or Watch and learn to see a mat woven for you.
rules: Each crossing is laid in the colour you choose; rows run left to right, from the start of the work.
The weave goes over two, under one, so the colours step across the rows.
The score counts the crossings that match the lit target, beyond what the plain fibre colour alone would give.
Undo takes back the last crossing.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
Watch and learn plays a whole round for you.
heritageNote: In the hills of the Dumbara valley in Sri Lanka, weavers build mats on a simple frame loom. Plant fibre is passed across a warp of dyed thread and beaten tight with a comb, and the stepped geometric patterns appear in black, red and natural colours as the rows are added.
